questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how XOR bitwise operations find the single non-duplicated number in an array. Mention time and space complexity.

rubric.criterion: Explains that x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, cancelling all duplicated pairs
States O(N) linear time complexity with single pass
States O(1) auxiliary space complexity with zero memory allocation

questions.modelAnswer: Bitwise XOR has the mathematical properties that x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x. When you XOR all numbers in the array together, every number that appears twice cancels out to zero. The single unique number remains unchanged. This finds the unique element in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary memory.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how the bitwise trick n & (n - 1) works. Explain how Brian Kernighan's algorithm uses it to count 1-bits.

rubric.criterion: Explains that n - 1 inverts the lowest set bit and all trailing zeros
Explains that n & (n - 1) clears exactly the lowest set bit in one operation
Notes that the loop runs in O(k) iterations where k is the number of set bits

questions.modelAnswer: Subtracting 1 from a number flips its lowest set 1-bit and all trailing zeros. When you compute n & (n - 1), that lowest 1-bit is cleared to zero while higher bits remain unchanged. Brian Kernighan's algorithm loops until n reaches zero. It counts set bits in O(k) iterations where k is the count of 1-bits.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain why cross-multiplication is preferred over slope division when testing if three points are collinear. Discuss two specific failure modes of slope division.

rubric.criterion: Explains division by zero failure mode for vertical lines where dx = 0
Explains floating-point precision truncation and rounding errors with Double slopes
Presents cross-multiplication formula: dy1 * dx2 == dy2 * dx1

questions.modelAnswer: Slope division has two major failure modes. First, vertical lines have dx = 0, causing a division by zero crash. Second, floating-point division introduces precision rounding errors where collinear slopes can appear unequal. Cross-multiplication with dy1 * dx2 == dy2 * dx1 keeps all operations in exact integer arithmetic and avoids division completely.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain the difference between remainder and modulo in Swift. How do you guarantee a positive modular result for circular index calculations?

rubric.criterion: Explains that % in Swift is remainder which preserves the sign of negative dividends
Provides the formula (n % m + m) % m to make sure modular results are non-negative
Explains relevance to circular buffers, collections, or carousel wrapping

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, the % operator computes remainder rather than mathematical modulo, so negative numbers produce negative results, such as (-1) % 5 returning -1. For circular buffers or carousel wrapping, indices must be non-negative. Writing (n % m + m) % m shifts negative remainders into the positive range from 0 to m minus 1.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how Swift OptionSet models bitmasks in iOS applications. Give an example of an Apple framework using OptionSet.

questions.modelAnswer: Swift's OptionSet protocol provides an idiomatic wrapper over raw bitmasks, packing multiple configuration flags into a single integer. It exposes convenient set syntax like contains, insert, and union without requiring raw bitwise operators. Apple frameworks use OptionSet extensively, such as UIView.AnimationOptions for animation curves and UIKeyModifierFlags for keyboard input.
